parsed.doc_summary: Law-firm blog post reporting that the Mass. SJC (Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893) removed Initiative Petition 25-21 (statewide rent cap) from the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-purpose exemption. G.L. c. 40P's ban on local rent control stays in place.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 - statewide rent increase cap (removed from ballot by SJC)
rules.requirement: The proposed ballot initiative would have repealed the ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5% for most rental units. The SJC ruled it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.quoted_span: annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.key_value: Lesser of CPI or 5% (never took effect)
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, facilities operated solely for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes.

no_rule_findings.finding: No statewide rent cap exists. The proposed cap (Initiative Petition 25-21) was blocked from the ballot, and the existing statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P) remains in force.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units.
